The Small Words That Get People to Reply

When nobody replies to your message, it's rarely the offer. It's the words around it. Small changes can make the difference between a message that gets ignored and one that gets an answer.

Say what you mean, with a reason

"Can you do me a favor?" gets a maybe. "Can you look at this because I'm stuck on one thing?" gives the person a reason, and a reason makes it easier to say yes.

Make the ask small

"Let's hop on a call to discuss" is a big ask. "Want me to send it over?" is a tiny one. People say yes to tiny. Ask for the next small step, not the whole sale.

Be specific

"Grow your business" is vague. "Get your first sale this month" is something a person can picture. Numbers, names and plain nouns beat adjectives every time.

Talk to one person

Write "you", not "people" or "businesses". Picture one reader. Sentences get shorter and warmer without any effort.

  • Add one reason to every ask.
  • Shrink the ask until it's easy to say yes to.
  • Replace one vague word with a specific one.
  • Cut anything you would not say out loud.

I keep a list of the words I use when I want someone to reply, call or buy, with examples of how they sound in real messages. It's free, and it's short enough to use today.
